program: Survivor housing, counseling, legal advocacy and violence prevention

what: Human Options provides emergency shelter, housing support, counseling and legal advocacy for people affected by relationship violence in Orange County.
Community centers, English/Spanish empowerment groups and care navigation help survivors seek safety and rebuild practical stability.

Its service model combines immediate crisis response with longer-term support; the numerical review covers conditional counseling, safety and household-resource effects rather than its full portfolio.
strengths: Shelter and housing navigation provide a concrete route away from unsafe conditions.
Counseling and legal advocacy address both emotional recovery and practical barriers to stability.
External randomized advocacy evidence supports plausible finite health mechanisms, alongside verified operating scale and original finances.
reservations: Reported support and safe-haven totals do not establish distinct adult completions or causal housing retention.
Clinical transfer, utility, ordinary-gift responsiveness and household resource incidence remain judgment-led.
Relocation, retaliation, foregone resources and external payer costs could offset gains; current unrestricted donor bottlenecks are unverified.

sections.what:
Human Options (EIN 95-3667817) operates residential and community services in Orange County. The [current services page](https://humanoptions.org/get-help/) describes shelter, counseling, legal advocacy, personal empowerment, care management and prevention. Its family resource centers serve several Orange County communities. CalOptima enrollment is required for its enhanced care management pathway; this is not a general insurance-free clinical program.

The [FY 2025 annual report](https://humanoptions.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Human-Options-Annual-Report-2024-2025_FINAL-1.pdf) reports 1,200 individuals receiving broadly described healing support and 498 survivors and families finding safe haven. Those are scale anchors, not verified treatment completions. They are not simply added: the model discounts eligibility and repeated or overlapping beneficiaries.
sections.monitoring:
The annual report's 90% safe-housing-at-exit claim has no public comparison group or long-term retention denominator. Hotline calls, knowledge gains and referrals are not separately credited as health. The current homepage's 2025 hotline total differs from the fiscal-year report, so neither is used as a unique-client denominator.

For a donor-sensitive evaluation, request distinct clients by age, program and residence; completed counseling intensity; safety and stable housing after exit; validated symptom and utility outcomes; and adverse events. Follow everyone offered services, including those who leave early, and compare against available public and nonprofit alternatives. Track the actual staff, rent assistance or other bottleneck that ordinary funds can change. [Current operations](https://humanoptions.org/)
sections.qualitative:
The [PATH randomized trial](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0205485) tested specialist psychological sessions added to ordinary domestic-violence advocacy. At twelve months, 29% versus 46% exceeded the depression threshold, but only 64% were followed up. There was no demonstrated reduction in further abuse or improvement in physical health. This supports a mental-health mechanism, not a claim that Human Options implements the same intervention or achieves its result.

The [post-shelter advocacy trial](https://cap.vaw.msu.edu/wp-content/uploads/2014/05/Two-year-followup-CAP-JCCP.pdf) found 24% versus 11% free from further physical violence over two years. It involved intensive ten-week advocacy for adult women after shelter; transferring this result to mixed residential records requires a substantial adjustment. The [Domestic Violence Housing First study](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2806371) also found better housing and mental-health outcomes, but was observational despite weighting and adjustment. Its scale scores are not QALYs and are not added as another benefit.

The [current PEP description](https://humanoptions.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/updated-PEP-flyer-2026.pdf) is a ten-week psychoeducational group, not proof of PATH-style psychological treatment. Counseling, housing and advocacy may overlap in the same person's recovery; the model explicitly reduces double counting. Safety, dignity and legal rights have value beyond the priced health component. PATH reported serious adverse events among 22 women (15 intervention, seven control), with association unclear for three women/four events. That imbalance is not converted into a causal harm rate; a separate hypothetical adverse case preserves potential harm without inventing an empirical bound. Only positive clinical contributions receive the overlap adjustment; negative health effects remain full.
sections.cost:
The original FY2025 return confirms full-recipient gross accrual expense of $7,595,219: Part IX $7,312,028 plus separately netted event costs $283,191. FY2024 gross expense is $8,075,513 and FY2023 $7,094,996; mean $7,588,576. No netted rental, gaming or inventory cost addback was found. These are annual operating costs across programs and overhead, not a restricted counseling price or verified marginal service queue. The annual report uses $7,306,512 expenses and $7,001,134 revenue with a restricted-revenue release explanation; those differently presented totals do not replace the original full expense denominator. Audit reconciliation and unrecognized volunteer/provider time remain unknown.

Clinical benefit is unchanged from the initial conditional estimate: 1.7010274295 LA QALYs. Signed household resources subtract 0.6934827280 welfare equivalents, leaving 1.0075447015 combined equivalents and about $75.38 million per ten, versus $44.65 million health-only. This increase comes from explicit resource judgments, not an observed negative Human Options effect or complete portfolio ranking. At $10,000 conditional linear funding share, the model gives 0.00223960 clinical QALYs and -0.00091305 signed income equivalents.

Clinical counseling uses 1,200 broad support records × 0.5 distinct eligible/intensity equivalents × 0.5 effect transfer × 0.5 funding response × 0.17 external depression-threshold difference × 0.15 judged utility × 0.5 year, discounted one year. Residential safety uses 498 mixed survivor/family records × 0.5 adult equivalents × 0.5 transfer × 0.5 funding response × 0.13 external two-year risk difference × 0.1 utility × 0.5 year, discounted two years. A positive-only 0.8 overlap adjustment and 0.95 LA/Orange residence share follow. Finite endpoint benefits are not annual episodes, permanent remission, mortality or extra survivor wages.

The separate resource ledger assumes 300 additional adult community-service households (1,200 × 0.5 resource adult/unique share × 0.5 capacity) and 124.5 residential households (498 × 0.5 household share × 0.5 capacity). These shares are independent of clinical efficacy; costs persist if clinical transfer or utility is zero. One survivor participant per distinct household and one welfare person are modeled; children and other household-member welfare remain unpriced. Half the residential households overlap community care: 62.25 joint, 237.75 community-only and 62.25 residential-only. No separate log gains are added for the same household.

Each community household incurs a judged $100 net time, travel, childcare or care-engagement burden. Each residential household has a conditional $1,200 annual net housing/food consumption relief hypothesis, not an observed grant, rent saving or wage. Tax/benefit withdrawal, displaced alternative aid and private spending offsets are already net within that hypothesis; only its positive portion is discounted 50% for overlapping safety/health value. The full $600 moving, disrupted work and other out-of-pocket burden remains: central residential net is zero, joint net −$100, community-only −$100. A $20,000 annual disposable-household baseline and one resource year after a one-year delay at 3% are material priors, not measured incomes. No retail shelter service value is added on top of health without the overlap adjustment.

Positive-resource stresses raise the net relief hypothesis to $3,000 before positive overlap; adverse stresses remove relief and raise displacement/moving costs to $2,000. Negative relief receives no overlap discount. The positive case is paired with a $500 per unique service-household institutional opportunity-cost hypothesis allocated across 100 distinct payer persons at $50,000 baseline; this matched case retains a positive net income-equivalent component. Another pairs positive relief with $100 net landlord margin per residential household across twenty separate one-person owner households at $60,000 baseline. Counterparty margins are net of their costs, not gross rent receipts; losses are included in a symmetric negative case. These are fiscal/provider incidence hypotheses, not donor utility or observed subsidy assignments. Actual partner-care, landlord, public-payer and nonlocal incidence remain unknown; neutral central anchors are not factual zeros. The conditional headline is partial household/health welfare, not complete social EV.

Clinical-null and financial-only preserve all resource costs; complete/income unknown remains null rather than zero. Zero expansion gives no new services, resources or health. Clinical harm stress is hypothetical and not inferred from the trial's adverse-event imbalance. Two-year resource stress assumes recurrent annual exposure, not a verified lasting resource effect.
sections.funding:
Original [FY 2023](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/953667817/202343139349304879/full), [FY 2024](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/953667817/202402999349301655/full) and [FY 2025](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/953667817/202513089349302841/full) returns all select accrual accounting. Part IX expenses plus separately netted event costs are $7,094,996, $8,075,513 and $7,595,219, averaging $7,588,576. No separate netted rental, gaming or inventory costs were reported. These are full-recipient Form 990 costs, not a verified marginal cash budget.

In FY 2025, government contributions were $3,981,606. Part IX allocates $5,877,004 to programs, $1,042,079 to management and $392,945 to fundraising, before $283,191 of direct event costs. Residential and community services account for $5,458,074 of program expenses; their scale is material, but that allocation does not identify an extra gift's use. The return reports $6,459,250 net assets without donor restrictions, not all held in cash.

The return's $895,341 revenue-expense deficit differs from the $305,378 net-asset decline because it separately reports $430,963 unrealized investment gains and $159,000 other changes. The annual report uses different revenue and expense presentation. A listed audit could not be downloaded in this review, so its reconciliation and opinion are not asserted. Historical deficits alone do not prove an immediate staffing gap.

The PEP flyer identifies FaCT public funding, while the current care-management service is tied to CalOptima. Existing contracts and other providers remain in the counterfactual. Ordinary donations might pay unreimbursed counseling, flexible assistance or continuity, but no costed incremental queue or current matched-gift offer was verified. The [donation page](https://humanoptions.org/donate/) was inspected without a transaction.

model.geographicAttribution: LA MSA consists of Los Angeles and Orange counties. Headquarters location alone does not establish allocation.
model.formula: QT=Np*dp*rp*b*ep*up*Tp/(1+d)^counselingDelay; QS=Ns*ds*rs*b*es*us*Ts/(1+d)^safetyDelay. H(x)=k*max(x,0)+min(x,0); QLA=g*[H(QT)+H(QS)−full hypothetical harm]. Separate capacity-based resource cohorts net joint same-HH resources BEFORE log; signed income=.5*persons*discounted finite years*log(1+net/baseline)*g. Price10=10*C/(QLA+income).
model.counterfactual: Public grants, CalOptima, other domestic-violence providers, ordinary advocacy, family support and existing reserves continue. The external counseling effect is already relative to ordinary advocacy, and the safety effect is relative to post-shelter usual services. b reduces added throughput for financing/provider replacement; rp and rs separately reduce clinical transfer. Past housing exits and advocacy successes are not newly purchased benefits.
model.attribution: dp discounts mixed ages, intensity and participant definitions before applying the adult psychological reference. ds translates mixed residential person/family records into adult index-person equivalents; no family-size multiplier is used. k reduces overlap between mental-health recovery and safety in the same survivors. No second physical-abuse or housing-first health effect is stacked on these terms.
model.uncertainty: Conditional reference rather than calibrated posterior or complete portfolio EV. Clinical utilities, finite benefit areas, net resources and funding response remain judgments. Null clinical keeps financial costs; unknown combined results remain null.
model.nativeOutcomes: Central modeled counseling 600 eligible/intensity-equivalent adults, 300 funding-responsive, 25.5 external-equivalent depression-threshold improvements. sections.what:
Human Options (EIN 95-3667817) operates residential and community services in Orange County. The [current services page](https://humanoptions.org/get-help/) describes shelter, counseling, legal advocacy, personal empowerment, care management and prevention. Its family resource centers serve several Orange County communities. CalOptima enrollment is required for its enhanced care management pathway; this is not a general insurance-free clinical program.

The [FY 2025 annual report](https://humanoptions.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Human-Options-Annual-Report-2024-2025_FINAL-1.pdf) reports 1,200 individuals receiving broadly described healing support and 498 survivors and families finding safe haven. Those are scale anchors, not verified treatment completions. They are not simply added: the model discounts eligibility and repeated or overlapping beneficiaries.
sections.monitoring:
The annual report's 90% safe-housing-at-exit claim has no public comparison group or long-term retention denominator. Hotline calls, knowledge gains and referrals are not separately credited as health. The current homepage's 2025 hotline total differs from the fiscal-year report, so neither is used as a unique-client denominator.

For a donor-sensitive evaluation, request distinct clients by age, program and residence; completed counseling intensity; safety and stable housing after exit; validated symptom and utility outcomes; and adverse events. Follow everyone offered services, including those who leave early, and compare against available public and nonprofit alternatives. Track the actual staff, rent assistance or other bottleneck that ordinary funds can change. [Current operations](https://humanoptions.org/)
sections.qualitative:
The [PATH randomized trial](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0205485) tested specialist psychological sessions added to ordinary domestic-violence advocacy. At twelve months, 29% versus 46% exceeded the depression threshold, but only 64% were followed up. There was no demonstrated reduction in further abuse or improvement in physical health. This supports a mental-health mechanism, not a claim that Human Options implements the same intervention or achieves its result.

The [post-shelter advocacy trial](https://cap.vaw.msu.edu/wp-content/uploads/2014/05/Two-year-followup-CAP-JCCP.pdf) found 24% versus 11% free from further physical violence over two years. It involved intensive ten-week advocacy for adult women after shelter; transferring this result to mixed residential records requires a substantial adjustment. The [Domestic Violence Housing First study](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2806371) also found better housing and mental-health outcomes, but was observational despite weighting and adjustment. Its scale scores are not QALYs and are not added as another benefit.

The [current PEP description](https://humanoptions.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/updated-PEP-flyer-2026.pdf) is a ten-week psychoeducational group, not proof of PATH-style psychological treatment. Counseling, housing and advocacy may overlap in the same person's recovery; the model explicitly reduces double counting. Safety, dignity and legal rights have value beyond the priced health component.
sections.cost:
The conditional central component is about $44.7 million per ten LA QALYs, using $7,595,219 of recipient-wide gross annual expense. It covers modeled counseling and post-shelter safety benefits only. It is not a complete portfolio return or the cost of purchasing a restricted clinical program.

For counseling, 1,200 reported participants are reduced to 50% distinct people with relevant eligibility and sufficient service intensity. Half the external depression-threshold difference is retained, ordinary funding responsiveness is 50%, and a 0.15 utility improvement lasts half a year. The latter is a judgmental clinical conversion, not a utility measured in the trial. This gives 1.8567961165 discounted all-population QALYs before cross-program overlap.

For residential services, the mixed 498-person/family count is multiplied by 0.5 adult index-person equivalents per record. The external 13-percentage-point reduction in any repeat physical violence is halved for transfer, with the same 50% funding response. Avoiding repeat violence is assigned 0.10 utility for half a year, credited with a two-year delay because the external endpoint is at two years. This adds 0.3813978697 QALYs before overlap.

Retaining 80% after cross-program overlap and 95% for LA/Orange beneficiary residence yields 1.7010274295 LA QALYs. No homicide, suicide, lifetime cure, separate child multiplier or additional annual reabuse benefit is added. Stronger and weaker assumptions span approximately $1.9 million to $20.5 billion per ten QALYs, with zero and unquantified downside also possible; these are stress scenarios, not confidence bounds.
sections.funding:
Original [FY 2023](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/953667817/202343139349304879/full), [FY 2024](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/953667817/202402999349301655/full) and [FY 2025](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/953667817/202513089349302841/full) returns all select accrual accounting. Part IX expenses plus separately netted event costs are $7,094,996, $8,075,513 and $7,595,219, averaging $7,588,576. No separate netted rental, gaming or inventory costs were reported. These are full-recipient Form 990 costs, not a verified marginal cash budget.

In FY 2025, government contributions were $3,981,606. Part IX allocates $5,877,004 to programs, $1,042,079 to management and $392,945 to fundraising, before $283,191 of direct event costs. Residential and community services account for $5,458,074 of program expenses; their scale is material, but that allocation does not identify an extra gift's use. The return reports $6,459,250 net assets without donor restrictions, not all held in cash.

The return's $895,341 revenue-expense deficit differs from the $305,378 net-asset decline because it separately reports $430,963 unrealized investment gains and $159,000 other changes. The annual report uses different revenue and expense presentation. A listed audit could not be downloaded in this review, so its reconciliation and opinion are not asserted. Historical deficits alone do not prove an immediate staffing gap.

The PEP flyer identifies FaCT public funding, while the current care-management service is tied to CalOptima. Existing contracts and other providers remain in the counterfactual. Ordinary donations might pay unreimbursed counseling, flexible assistance or continuity, but no costed incremental queue or current matched-gift offer was verified. The [donation page](https://humanoptions.org/donate/) was inspected without a transaction.

sensitivity: The central price is approximately $44.7 million per ten LA QALYs. Halving ordinary-funding responsiveness doubles this price.

At current recipient cost, $1 million per ten QALYs requires 75.95219 additional LA QALYs; $100,000 requires 759.5219. These requirements exceed the modeled component but do not price the omitted portfolio.
Removing the post-shelter safety branch leaves the psychological component; no mortality or separate housing-first uplift replaces it.
External outcome thresholds are imperfect clinical summaries. If they do not imply a utility difference, that branch contributes no QALYs even if its legal or social outcome improves.
Primary financials include recognized noncash contributions; unrecognized volunteer time, survivor travel and external provider costs would require a separate societal analysis.
